1.why: Recovery records contain only token, flowId, expiry and attempt counters — there is no user/account store at all, so no ownership check between a reset code and a user is ever performed.

2.why: Because tokens are generated without any binding to an email/account, any session presenting the hex string succeeds (until the single-use flag is set), so the code is effectively not user-specific.

3.why: The /api/reset handler only sets session.resetComplete and rewrites the global passwordHash; no session invalidation or revocation of other session entries occurs, so pre-existing sessions in the `sessions` Map remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key, HSTS with preload is set, and plain HTTP only 308-redirects to HTTPS, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (relies on Bun/OpenSSL defaults, which are TLS 1.3-capable).

5.why: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id, but reset tokens are stored in the `recoveries` Map as raw plaintext hex values with no hashing or encryption, and no other user data is protected.

6.why: There is no real email delivery; the reset token is returned directly in the JSON API response as `mockToken` and written into the visible Logs panel and browser console, i.e. exposed rather than guarded.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated: conservative email regex plus 254-char cap, token regex /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/, password length caps and complexity policy, 2 KB bounded JSON body parsing with fatal UTF-8 decoding.

8.why: The only redirect is the HTTP listener's fixed 308 to `https://localhost:<HTTPS_PORT>` with no user-controlled destination, and CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: No email templates exist in the code; the only rendered dynamic values are the CSRF token/nonce injected via JSON.stringify, and client-side output uses textContent, so no user input is interpolated into HTML or scripts.

10.why: The client explicitly logs `[Mock delivery] Reset token: <token>` and `[Mock MFA delivery] Verification code: <code>` to the on-page Logs panel and console.log, directly exposing secrets.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed, but the MFA verification code "482916" is hard-coded twice in the source (returned to the client and compared server-side), so a secret does live in the code.

12.why: There is no username/password login, but the hard-coded static MFA code "482916" and the "initial-placeholder-value" seed hash function as fixed default credentials that are always accepted.

13.why: consumeRateLimit enforces 5 token verifications and 8 recovery requests per IP per 10-minute window with a 10-minute block, a 3-per-session recovery cap, and MFA failures ≥5 clear the flow with a 429.

14.why: /api/recovery returns the same generic "If an account can be recovered..." message and always mints a token regardless of input, and verify/reset errors are uniformly worded, so no existence oracle is provided.

15.why: Tokens are 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues (random and high-entropy) and single-use, but they are not tied to any user or email, so the user-specific part of the statement is false.
